round1.cite: the product owner can rely on a SHIP
round1.reply:
Yes

This implements the standing rules without over-specifying. It has a metric (SHIP gates resting on an unlabelled or blocked command: 1 of 1 on card 217, target 0 over three cards). It has counter-metrics against ceremony and gaming. It is limited to the next three gated cards, and its retro decides keep, revise or drop. It is a two-way door.

It also supports "open FAILs stop the line": a gate with no evidence becomes HOLD, not SHIP. That fits the product owner's accountability rule. The cost is small: one labelled list and one read of it. It adds no seat, no file and no up-front design, so the team returns to product value. The deferred checker and the seat-time cap are rightly left for later.

Those are specification issues, not reasons to block the trial.

round1.cite: We believe a gate that must label each check cannot say SHIP on air.
round1.reply:
Support-it

The rule is testable red first. Replaying the card 217 gate (every command blocked, verdict "SHIP") must fail under C2, and a gate with pasted output must pass. The trial is also a cheap two-way door.

Two gaps remain:
- The rule and C2 disagree. The PICK says "all blocked or unlabelled" means HOLD, while C2 says "no rerun line for any required command". A gate with one rerun and five record-only checks could pass either way.
- Nothing checks that the pasted output lines are real. The facilitator reads labels by eye, and the machine checker is deferred. The card 264 unsupported safety claim would also slip through if it is labelled record-only.

I'd tighten the wording before the first trial gate.

round1.cite: The facilitator's checklist reads the labels before the sign-off seat is briefed
round1.reply:
Support-it

The labels are committed in the gate report, so git can show whether each check was labelled. Two loopholes remain.

- **C2 is too weak.** It only blocks SHIP when no required command was rerun. One rerun line plus several "blocked" or unlabelled checks still passes. It should require that every required command is rerun, or record-only with the committed file named, or blocked with a HOLD verdict.
- **A "rerun" label can't be checked from git.** Pasted output could be invented. A checker that rejects a gate record with no command output lines is the better fix. It is already on the deferred list, so I'd move it up.
- **C3 is self-attested.** "SHIP on facilitator-run output" rests on the facilitator's own notes.
